requirements: Participation requires being a current national scholarship holder selected under one of the six calls listed in the requisites section.
The beneficiary must send the information and documentation the OAS requests for formalisation and disbursement, on time and in full.

The OAS will abstain from granting the support when it notes a restriction or incompatibility and, if already granted, will proceed to cancel it under the Reglamento.
Secihti will not intervene in the management of the migratory situation of the national scholarship holder or their economic dependents.

Distribucion geografica de la institucion receptora en Mexico.

official.application_route: No open application: Secihti nominates and validates eligible national scholarship holders and sends the list to the OEA, which selects and then formalises and disburses directly to the beneficiary.
official.citizenship_residency: Must declare in the single profile the nationality of one of the OAS Member States, with the exception of Mexico; double nationality and residence in Mexico are published selection criteria.
official.international_eligibility: Only non-Mexican nationals of OAS Member States are eligible; Mexican nationals are expressly excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must be admitted and enrolled in Fisica, Matematicas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biologia y Quimica, Ingenierias, Medicina y Ciencias de la Salud (excluding the training of medical specialties and subspecialties), Biotecnologia or Ciencias Agropecuarias.
official.duration: One-off payment (aporte unico) for gastos de instalacion; no support period is published beyond the single contribution.
official.description: The Secretaria de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnologia e Innovacion (Secihti) and the Organizacion de los Estados Americanos (OEA) call for professionals who are nationals of OAS Member States other than Mexico, in the listed science, engineering, health, biotechnology and agricultural areas, who obtained a Secihti National Scholarship under the six named calls, to compete for a complementary support. Its stated objective is to support the training of people and increase capacities in science, humanities, technology and innovation through complementary supports for settling-in expenses in Mexico.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not an award you can apply for in the ordinary sense: the only entry route published is already holding a current Secihti National Scholarship from one of six specific 2025/2026 calls and appearing on the list Secihti sent to the OEA on 28 August 2026. If you are on that list, the OEA money is a single USD 1,200 settling-in payment sent to your Mexican bank account in pesos at the exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, so your nominal USD figure will drift with the peso. Your real maintenance still comes from the separate Secihti National Scholarship under the Tabulador de Becas Nacionales 2026 plus ISSSTE medical cover, both of which the call states are independent of this OAS support.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Mexican nationals of OAS Member States who already hold a current Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in a listed STEM, health, biotechnology or agricultural-sciences area in Mexico.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you appear on the compliant list Secihti sent to the OEA on 28 August 2026; if you are not a current holder of one of the six named calls you cannot be considered.
Check you were admitted and enrolled (not just accepted) in one of the seven listed subject areas before the committee met on 3 September 2026.
Make sure your single-profile nationality declaration is an OAS Member State other than Mexico and that it matches your passport.
Watch for the OAS email requesting formalisation information between 7 and 18 September 2026 and reply the same day.
Have a Mexican bank account in your own name ready, since the OEA deposit is made in Mexican pesos to the beneficiary's account.
Keep a clean record on the S190 programme: any prior OEA complementary support, or any non-compliance report or outstanding debt, removes you from consideration.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply directly: there is no public form, so first-time applicants and people whose Secihti call is not one of the six named ones are outside the process entirely.
Being merely accepted rather than admitted and enrolled in the listed areas, or studying in a medical specialty/subspecialty track that is expressly excluded.
Missing the single emailed prevencion about incomplete documentation, which gives you at least five business days and can end in cancellation and reassignment of the support.
Holding a temporary or permanent resident card, or having a prior OEA complementary award, which are straightforward disqualifiers.
An S190 non-compliance report or outstanding debt that is only discovered at Secihti's validation stage.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition of any kind, international travel to Mexico, visa and immigration costs (Secihti states it will not manage your or your dependents' migratory situation), and all ordinary living expenses beyond the single settling-in payment, which comes from the separate Secihti National Scholarship monthly support and the ISSSTE medical service.
document_audit: No named document list is published, so do not assume which papers OAS will ask for: the request arrives by email and the term to answer is set by OAS but cannot be under five business days.
The deposit is made in Mexican pesos to a bank account in the beneficiary's name, so account holder name must match your formalisation paperwork exactly.
Your name will be published in the Secihti beneficiaries register once a support agreement has been formalised, and the award can be audited for five years after it ends.
alerts: The convocatoria warns that dates may be modified for justified reasons, with the modification notice published on the institutional portal, so re-check the OAS page rather than trusting a cached copy of the PDF.

Selection is not purely academic: ten criteria include geographic balance by country, your country's Human Development Index, gender, area of study, host-institution geography, doctorate over master's, double nationality and residence in Mexico, and the proportion of candidates per country.
If the support is cancelled or you decline it, the OAS reserves the right to reassign it to applicants who were not favoured for lack of budget, so the number of awards is not fixed.
A decision issued by the DGBACCYH on interpretation or unforeseen situations is definitive and unappealable, although ordinary legal remedies remain open.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secihti screens and nominates current national scholarship holders and hands the compliant list to the OEA, whose award committee selects and notifies directly; you only act once contacted, by signing the formalisation instrument and answering OAS's email request for banking and personal information, after which OAS disburses.

official.application_route: One online application through the COMEXUS system; no admission letter is required at application time, but grantees do not receive the award until admitted to a qualified programme.
official.citizenship_residency: US candidates; dual citizens may compete. Candidates studying, living or working in Mexico during the application process, and candidates holding a temporary or permanent resident card for Mexico, are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: No - this is a US-to-Mexico binational exchange award for US candidates; it is not open to non-US nationals.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of study are accepted except medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry.
official.research_requirement: Applicants proposing research involving human or animal subjects should have their projects reviewed by their home institution's Institutional Review Board (IRB); if selected, grantees may also need research clearance from the host institution, and affiliation letters should reflect the host institution's support in that process.
official.duration: Up to 2 academic years for a master's and up to 3 academic years for a PhD; all candidates receive an initial academic year of funding, with approval of subsequent support subject to academic performance and availability of funds.
official.description: COMEXUS offers US candidates the opportunity to complete a master's or PhD degree at a qualified academic institution in Mexico, funding up to two academic years for a master's and up to three for a PhD, with all candidates receiving an initial academic year of funding and later years subject to academic performance and availability of funds. Financial support comprises monthly maintenance, one round-trip international air ticket for the grantee, a Fulbright medical benefit plan, COMEXUS assistance with visa paperwork, and up to 50,000 pesos per academic year for tuition.
official.english_requirement: No English-language test is published. COMEXUS requires advanced Spanish and both a Language Self-Evaluation and a Foreign Language Evaluation completed by a qualified evaluator; failure to submit these forms makes the application ineligible, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in Spanish.

applicant_utility.summary: COMEXUS funds US citizens to take a master's or PhD at a qualified Mexican institution, paying monthly maintenance, a round-trip international air ticket, a Fulbright medical plan, visa paperwork help, and up to 50,000 pesos a year towards tuition. Applications for this cycle closed on 6 October 2026 at 5:00 PM EST, with shortlisted candidates interviewed in Spanish in March 2027 and grantees starting on their host institution's calendar, so the practical next window is the following year's call. Your biggest single hurdle is not the Fulbright application but the Mexican university: you apply to Fulbright without an admission letter, but you receive nothing until you are admitted to a qualified programme, and deferring the award to another year is not permitted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: US citizens with advanced Spanish and at least a B.S. or B.A. who want a master's or PhD in Mexico in any field other than medicine, veterinary medicine or dentistry.
application_readiness_checklist: Build a realistic target list of Mexican programmes and start contacting their academic departments early for the affiliation letter confirming the programme is available and admission is feasible.

Pre-book your language evaluator: both the Language Self-Evaluation and the Foreign Language Evaluation must be completed by a qualified evaluator, and a missing form makes the whole application ineligible.
Register your three recommenders in the online system well before the deadline, preferably with institutional email addresses, and warn them to expect the system-generated upload link.
Assemble transcripts for every degree-granting institution plus any other school where you took 12 or more credits that are not shown as transfer credits on your undergraduate transcript.

If the project involves human or animal subjects, get your home institution's IRB review done before the deadline and make sure the affiliation letter reflects host-institution support for research clearance.

Confirm you are not studying, living or working in Mexico while applying and hold no temporary or permanent Mexican resident card, then map your university admission calendar against the grant start date you name.
common_rejection_risks: Omitting either language form, which is an automatic ineligibility rather than a scoring penalty.
Counting on the award before admission: grantees receive nothing until admitted to a qualified programme, and no deferral to a different year is allowed.
Losing eligibility during the process by studying, living or working in Mexico, or by acquiring a temporary or permanent resident card.
Choosing medicine, veterinary medicine or dentistry, which are excluded from all fields.
A Statement of Grant Purpose that does not justify the choice of country and institution or demonstrate that Spanish is genuinely advanced enough to complete the project.
Recommenders who never register in the system, so the three letters are simply absent at the deadline.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above the 50,000-peso annual ceiling, which at private or high-fee institutions can be substantial; Mexican university application, tuition-deposit and enrolment fees; visa and consular costs beyond COMEXUS's paperwork assistance; relocation and settling-in beyond the single orientation; and costs for dependants, since only the grantee's air ticket and medical benefit are funded.
document_audit: The Foreign Language Evaluation must be done by a qualified evaluator, not self-assessed, and the two language forms are treated as a completeness gate, so confirm they are uploaded rather than merely promised.

Transcripts are required for non-degree study of 12 or more credits that is not reflected as a transfer credit on the undergraduate transcript, so a single semester abroad can create an extra transcript request that catches applicants out.

The affiliation letter is a letter of feasibility and availability from the host academic department, which is not the same as the formal admission letter required before the grant offer; keep both in view.

IRB clearance sits with your US home institution, and host-institution research clearance may be a separate step after selection, so start the ethics review early if your project uses human or animal subjects.
alerts: The call for this cycle closed on 6 October 2026 at 5:00 PM EST; do not plan around a late or rolling submission, as COMEXUS publishes a hard closing date and time.

Most Mexican universities have not opened their own admission calls when the Fulbright call closes, so an acceptance letter is not required at application time, but the sequencing risk stays with you.
Years two and three of funding are not guaranteed: continuation is subject to academic performance and the availability of funds.
Grantees with August or September start dates must attend the mandatory COMEXUS welcome orientation in Mexico City in the last week of August 2027, so budget travel into that window.
Interviews for shortlisted candidates are conducted in Spanish, so treat speaking fluency, not just paperwork, as part of the assessment.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one complete online application with all uploads by the deadline, then COMEXUS shortlists and interviews candidates in Spanish in March 2027, after which selected candidates apply to a Mexican university and present the admission letter before the grant start date to activate the award.
